title: PARDIG & SatWeave: Foundational Datasets for Earth Science
gist: Google DeepMind openly releases SatWeave (an hourly, 17-channel global geostationary satellite mosaic) and PARDIG (an AI precipitation reanalysis trained on NASA GPM radar, 15-min/~10 km), the two datasets behind WeatherNext 3, with live feeds and historical archives on Google Cloud Storage and Earth Engine. PARDIG reportedly beats NASA's IMERG-Final by more than 30% on hourly light-to-moderate rain detection. The text says SatWeave combines five satellites but a caption says six.

insights.claim: Google DeepMind's SatWeave dataset fuses geostationary imagery from GOES-East, GOES-West, Meteosat 0, Meteosat Indian Ocean and Himawari into one global mosaic across 17 visible, water vapor and infrared channels, while most existing global composites offer four or fewer channels or update only every few hours.
insights.speaker: WeatherNext team
insights.so_what: A free, harmonized multi-sensor satellite feed lowers the data-engineering barrier for weather startups and erodes the moat of vendors selling cleaned satellite composites.
insights.quote: Most existing global composites drop incompatible aspects, offering only four or fewer channels, or updating every few hours.
insights.locator: SatWeave: A unified view of Earth from space

insights.claim: Harmonizing geostationary satellites is hard because each uses different map projections, file formats, sensors and scan schedules ranging from 10 to 30 minutes.
insights.speaker: WeatherNext team
insights.so_what: Data harmonization is a real engineering moat; Google giving it away commoditizes a layer of the weather-data value chain.
insights.locator: SatWeave combines imagery from five satellites

insights.claim: Because SatWeave updates hourly, WeatherNext 3 can issue new global forecasts every hour, unlike models initialized on analysis data that is refreshed only every six hours.
insights.speaker: WeatherNext team
insights.so_what: Hourly-refresh global AI forecasts beat six-hourly NWP cycles on timeliness, which matters for weather-sensitive trading (power, gas, ags) and nowcasting.
insights.quote: SatWeave updates hourly and thus allows WeatherNext 3 to produce new global predictions, in contrast to models initialized on analysis data refreshed every six hours.
insights.locator: SatWeave updates hourly and thus allows

insights.claim: Google is releasing SatWeave as an hourly live feed plus a historical archive covering more than a decade, and wants to explore solar power and wildfire monitoring applications with outside researchers and developers.
insights.speaker: WeatherNext team
insights.so_what: Watch for solar generation nowcasting and wildfire-risk products (utilities, insurers) built on SatWeave cloud imagery.
insights.quote: we're eager to explore forecasting applications such as solar power and wildfire monitoring

insights.claim: PARDIG (Precipitation AI Reanalysis: Densely Inferred GPM) is trained directly on sparse spaceborne radar observations from NASA's GPM Core Observatory, using SatWeave imagery and ECMWF atmospheric fields as inputs, on an AI architecture similar to WeatherNext 3.
insights.speaker: WeatherNext team
insights.so_what: Densifying sparse but accurate satellite radar with AI is a template for building global ground-truth datasets without ground infrastructure.

insights.claim: PARDIG produces a global precipitation map at 15-minute temporal resolution and about 10-kilometer spatial resolution, with an average latency of about five hours.
insights.speaker: WeatherNext team
insights.so_what: Five-hour latency makes it near-real-time monitoring rather than nowcasting; useful for crop, flood and parametric-insurance triggers.
insights.locator: The result is a highly accurate

insights.claim: In evaluations against radar networks in the US, Europe and Japan and over 36,000 weather stations, PARDIG outperforms leading global baselines at all analyzed rain rates and improves hourly light-to-moderate precipitation detection skill over NASA's IMERG-Final by more than 30%.
insights.speaker: WeatherNext team
insights.so_what: A free AI dataset beating the standard research-quality NASA product could become the new default input for rainfall-dependent models in agriculture, hydrology and insurance.
insights.quote: PARDIG improves hourly precipitation detection skill over IMERG-Final by more than 30% on light-to-moderate precipitation.
insights.locator: We have performed evaluations of PARDIG

insights.claim: According to Google DeepMind, PARDIG is particularly good at capturing extreme precipitation, which existing global products can struggle to detect, as shown in a comparison during the July 2025 Texas Hill Country flash floods.
insights.speaker: WeatherNext team
insights.so_what: Better detection of extreme rain is directly relevant to flood risk pricing, cat-bond modeling and disaster response.
insights.quote: It proved particularly effective at capturing extreme precipitation, which can be challenging for existing global products to detect.

insights.claim: Because PARDIG learns from satellites rather than relying only on ground measurements, its developers expect reliable accuracy everywhere on Earth, including regions without ground radars or dense rain-gauge networks.
insights.speaker: WeatherNext team
insights.so_what: This is an expectation, since validation was done only in radar-rich US, Europe and Japan; the payoff is in data-poor emerging markets for ag and insurance, but it is not yet proven there.
insights.quote: we expect it to have reliable accuracy everywhere on Earth, even in areas where these measurements are not available.
insights.locator: Because PARDIG learns directly from satellites

themes.theme: Open release and Google Earth AI strategy

insights.claim: Google is releasing PARDIG historical archives from 1999 to 2026 plus a live feed, and SatWeave live and historical data, openly on Google Cloud Storage, with PARDIG historical catalogs also in Google Earth Engine, as part of Google's Earth AI portfolio.
insights.speaker: WeatherNext team
insights.so_what: Open data hosted on Google Cloud pulls the climate and weather developer ecosystem toward Google's cloud and Earth Engine; it is a cloud-adoption play disguised as open science.
insights.locator: Empowering the weather and climate ecosystem

insights.claim: Google DeepMind plans to work with outside groups on better flood, landslide and drought models built on PARDIG, especially in regions without dense ground radar networks.
insights.speaker: WeatherNext team
insights.so_what: Watch for hydrology and climate-risk products (parametric insurance, development-finance risk tools) aimed at the Global South that use PARDIG.
insights.locator: Along with the live data feed

insights.claim: Google's AI weather work depends on public satellite and data programs from ECMWF, NASA, JAXA, NOAA, EUMETSAT, KMA, JMA and KNMI, plus Synoptic Data, so its products sit on top of government-funded observing infrastructure.
insights.speaker: WeatherNext team
insights.so_what: Cuts to public observing systems such as GPM or GOES would be an upstream risk for AI weather models built by private firms.
